meta.description: Loading of outstanding authorization data from sequential files into the IMS database for recovery or initial population of the pending authorization database.
meta.process_description: The program PAUDBLOD is the counterpart to the unload program PAUDBUNL and reads two sequential input files: one containing authorization summary records (root segments) and one containing authorization detail records (child segments). First, all root segments (authorization summaries per account) are read sequentially and inserted as parent segments into the IMS database. Subsequently, all child segments (authorization details) are read; for each detail record, the corresponding root record is first located in the IMS database by account ID, and then the detail record is inserted as a child segment. Already existing records (duplicates) are tolerated and logged without triggering an abend.

files.INFILE1: Sequential input file with authorization summary records (root segments, PAUTSUM0) per credit card account
files.INFILE2: Sequential input file with authorization detail records (child segments, PAUTDTL1) with account ID as key and detail data for individual authorizations

business_rules: Root segments (authorization summaries) must be loaded into the IMS database before child segments (authorization details), as required by the hierarchical IMS structure.
For each child record, the associated root record must be locatable in the IMS database by account ID (ACCNTID) before the detail record can be inserted.
Duplicates (status 'II' = Duplicate Segment) are tolerated and logged for both root and child segments, but do not cause program termination – this enables idempotent restart runs.
Child records with a non-numeric account ID are skipped and not loaded into the database.
Any other database error (other than duplicate or success) causes an immediate program abend (ABEND) to ensure data consistency.
The program operates in IMS batch mode with PSB scheduling and supports checkpoint/restart mechanisms for restartability in case of errors.

variables.name: QUAL-SSA-KEY-VALUE
variables.description: The 11-digit account ID used as the search key for qualified IMS database access. This value is used to build the qualified SSA (Segment Search Argument) in order to specifically locate the root segment record (PAUTSUM0) of a particular credit card account in the IMS database before inserting associated detail records.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The closing parenthesis ')' of the qualified IMS SSA (Segment Search Argument). It forms the syntactically required end of the SSA search condition, e.g. 'PAUTSUM0(ACCNTID  = 00012345678)'. Without this character, the IMS search expression would be syntactically invalid.

variables.name: ROOT-UNQUAL-SSA
variables.description: Unqualified Segment Search Argument (SSA) for accessing the root segment PAUTSUM0 (authorization summary per credit card account) in the IMS database. An unqualified SSA contains no key filter and is used when navigating sequentially across all root segments without specifying a particular account key.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The IMS segment name 'PAUTSUM0', which identifies the root segment of the pending authorization database. This name tells IMS which segment type (authorization summary per account) the database access is targeting.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing space of the unqualified SSA for the root segment. According to IMS SSA syntax, a space at this position signals that no further qualification (no key filter) follows — the access is therefore performed without restriction to a specific account key.

variables.name: CHILD-UNQUAL-SSA
variables.description: Unqualified Segment Search Argument (SSA) for accessing the child segment PAUTDTL1 (authorization detail record) in the IMS database. Used to access the subordinate individual authorization transactions within an already-positioned root segment, without specifying an additional key filter.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The IMS segment name 'PAUTDTL1', which identifies the child segment of the pending authorization database. This name tells IMS that the access targets the detail record of an individual authorization transaction (subordinate to the account root segment).

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing space of the unqualified SSA for the child segment. Signals to IMS, in accordance with SSA syntax, that no key filter is specified for the detail record — access is performed relative to the current database position (below the already-positioned root segment).

variables.name: PRM-INFO
variables.description: Group field for all control parameters of the batch load run. Contains the configurable runtime parameters that govern the program's behavior with respect to expiration deadlines, checkpoint frequency, and diagnostic output. These parameters are typically passed via JCL SYSIN or a parameter record.

variables.name: P-EXPIRY-DAYS
variables.description: Configuration parameter: Specifies the number of days after which a pending authorization is considered expired and should no longer be loaded into the IMS database. Controls the validity check during loading — authorizations whose age exceeds this threshold are skipped in order to avoid stale holds on credit limits.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter between parameter fields in the input parameter record. Serves to correctly position the subsequent parameters within the parameter string and carries no business meaning of its own.

variables.name: P-CHKP-FREQ
variables.description: Checkpoint frequency: Specifies the number of processed records after which the program issues an IMS checkpoint. Checkpoints preserve processing progress so that, in the event of a program failure, the load run does not have to restart from the beginning but can resume from the last checkpoint (restart capability).

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter between parameter fields in the input parameter record. Serves to correctly position the subsequent parameters within the parameter string and carries no business meaning of its own.

variables.name: P-CHKP-DIS-FREQ
variables.description: Display checkpoint frequency: Specifies the number of processed records after which intermediate statistics (e.g. number of records read, written, and skipped) are written to the log. Enables monitoring of load progress during batch processing without affecting the actual checkpoint mechanism.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter between parameter fields in the input parameter record. Serves to correctly position the subsequent parameters within the parameter string and carries no business meaning of its own.

variables.name: P-DEBUG-FLAG
variables.description: Control switch for extended diagnostic output: When set to 'Y', the program writes additional technical detail information (e.g. IMS status codes, processed key values, intermediate results) to the log. Facilitates error analysis when problems occur during the load run without impacting production operation (where it is set to 'N').

variables.name: DEBUG-ON
variables.description: Condition name: True when debug mode is active (P-DEBUG-FLAG = 'Y'). Allows the program code to check in a readable way whether extended diagnostic output is enabled for error analysis of the load run.

variables.name: DEBUG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name: True when debug mode is inactive (P-DEBUG-FLAG = 'N'). Allows the program code to check in a readable way whether the load run is operating in normal production mode without additional diagnostic output.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing filler at the end of the parameter record. Serves to correctly align the overall length of the parameter field and carries no business meaning of its own.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY
variables.description: Working storage area for an authorization summary record (root segment) of a credit card account. Via the included copybook CIPAUSMY, it contains all fields of the IMS root segment PAUTSUM0: account ID, customer ID, authorization status, credit limit, cash limit, current balances, and counters and amounts for approved and declined authorizations. It is populated when reading from INFILE1 and subsequently written as the root segment to the IMS database.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS
variables.description: Working storage area for an authorization detail record (child segment) of an individual credit card transaction. Via the included copybook CIPAUDTY, it contains all fields of the IMS child segment PAUTDTL1: authorization key (date/time), card number, authorization type, card expiry date, transaction amount, approved amount, response code, and merchant and country identifiers. It is populated when reading from INFILE2 and, after the associated root segment has been successfully located, inserted as a child segment into the IMS database.

variables.name: IO-PCB-MASK
variables.description: Placeholder mask for the IMS I/O Program Communication Block (IO-PCB). The IO-PCB is the interface between the COBOL batch program and the IMS runtime system for system services such as issuing checkpoints (CHKP call) and restart operations. This simplified declaration as a single character serves the purpose of formally addressing the IO-PCB in the ENTRY interface of the IMS batch program.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central control paragraph of the load program PAUDBLOD and orchestrates the complete business process: initialization, sequential loading of all authorization summaries (root segments) and then all authorization details (child segments) into the IMS database, followed by an orderly program termination.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.description: Initializes the batch load run by determining and logging the current processing date and opening the two input files containing the authorization data for processing.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the initialization section (1000-INIT). Serves as a structural return point after completion of all preparatory steps for the database load process.

paragraphs.name: 2000-READ-ROOT-SEG-FILE
paragraphs.description: Sequentially reads the authorization summary records (root segments) per credit card account from the input file and controls their transfer into the IMS database or detects end of file.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the root segment load process (paragraph 2000). Serves as the structural end point of the processing loop for authorization summary records.

paragraphs.name: 2100-INSERT-ROOT-SEG
paragraphs.description: This paragraph stores an authorization summary record (root segment) as a parent entry per credit card account in the IMS database. It ensures that duplicates are tolerated and genuine errors are handled by a controlled program abort.

paragraphs.name: 2100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of processing section 2100, which marks the end of the root segment load processing and enables the return to the parent control flow.

paragraphs.name: 3000-READ-CHILD-SEG-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls the sequential reading of authorization detail records (child segments) and forwards each valid record for insertion into the IMS database. It ensures that only records with a valid numeric account ID are processed and correctly detects end of file.

paragraphs.name: 3000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the root segment load loop (3000-series paragraph group). Serves as a structural return point after completion of the processing of an authorization summary record.

paragraphs.name: 3100-INSERT-CHILD-SEG
paragraphs.description: This paragraph is responsible for inserting a single authorization detail record (child segment) into the IMS database by first checking whether the associated account summary (root segment) exists before inserting the detail record as a hierarchical subordinate.

paragraphs.name: 3100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the root segment load process (paragraph 3100). Serves as the structural end point of the processing loop for authorization summary records and enables a clean return after completion of root segment processing.

paragraphs.name: 3200-INSERT-IMS-CALL
paragraphs.description: This paragraph inserts a single authorization detail record (child segment) as a subordinate element into the IMS database and evaluates the result: success, duplicate, or critical error with program abort.

paragraphs.name: 3200-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of processing section 3200, which ensures an orderly return to the calling control logic of the load process.

paragraphs.name: 4000-FILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: After completion of the load process, properly closes both sequential input files (root segments and detail segments) and logs any errors during closing without aborting the process.

paragraphs.name: 4000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the load process for root segments. This paragraph serves as the structural end point of the processing loop and enables a clean return after completion of all database load operations.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND
paragraphs.description: Controlled program abort in the event of critical database errors: signals a severe error during the IMS load operation to the batch system in order to ensure data consistency of the pending authorization database and prevent uncontrolled further processing.

paragraphs.name: 9999-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal exit point of the program PAUDBLOD, serving as a structured return point after completion of all load and logging activities.
